label: Release, promotion, signing, and dependency management

map.subsystem: Release, promotion, signing, and dependency management (GlycemicGPT android-unofficial)

capabilities.name: Promotion pipeline topology (develop -> main)
capabilities.behavior: Two long-lived branches. All contributor PRs target `develop` (squash-merged); `main` is release-only. A maintainer promotes with `gh pr create --base main --head develop --title "chore: promote develop to main"`, merged as a real merge commit (not squash) to preserve ancestry. That single push to `main` fans out to three workflows keyed off `github.event.head_commit.message`: release.yml (version + signed APK), changelog-pr.yml (CHANGELOG PR), sync-main-to-develop.yml (cherry-pick back). Loop avoidance is entirely message-string based: changelog fires on `promote develop to main` and NOT on `[Changelog]`/`chore: release`; sync fires ONLY on `chore: release` or `[Changelog] Update CHANGELOG.md`; so the promotion commit never re-triggers sync and the bot commits never re-trigger the changelog. Documented status: built, unit-proven in parts, never exercised end-to-end live.

capabilities.name: release.yml job graph and gating
capabilities.behavior: Triggers: push to `main`, plus workflow_dispatch. Concurrency `release-${github.ref}`, cancel-in-progress false. Top-level `permissions: contents: read` — every write uses a scoped GitHub App token; read-only checkouts set `persist-credentials: false`. Jobs: (1) release-please; (2) auto-merge-release, `if: needs.release-please.outputs.pr != ''`; (3) detect-deployable-changes, `if release_created != 'true' && pr == '' && head_commit.message contains 'promote develop to main'`; (4) fallback-release, same condition AND `has_deployable_changes == 'true'`; (5) release-android-apk, `if: always() && !cancelled() && !contains(needs.*.result,'failure') && (release-please.release_created=='true' || fallback-release.release_created=='true')`. Jobs 1,2,4,5 declare `environment: release-gated`, which holds the only copies of the RELEASE/MERGE app keys and pauses each run for a required-reviewer approval.

capabilities.name: release-please configuration and version scheme
capabilities.behavior: release-please-action v4.4.1 (SHA 5c625bfb5d1ff62eadeeb3772007f7f66fdcf071) with `release-please-config.json` + `.release-please-manifest.json`. Config: bootstrap-sha `53bd47b72639ccf7fc132a7a1e33265e0d744042`; single package `.`; release-type `simple`; package-name `glycemicgpt-android-unofficial`; `bump-minor-pre-major: true`; draft false; prerelease false; `include-component-in-tag: false`; `include-v-in-tag: true` (tags are `vX.Y.Z`); PR title pattern `chore: release ${version}`; extra-files = app/, wear-device/, watchface/ `build.gradle.kts`. Manifest currently `{".": "0.14.0"}`. Each module carries `val appVersionName = "0.14.0" // x-release-please-version`; versionCode is derived in Gradle as `major*1_000_000 + minor*10_000 + patch`. Conventional-commit visibility: feat/fix/perf/docs/refactor/ci visible in CHANGELOG; chore/test hidden. release-type `simple` also makes release-please the owner of CHANGELOG.md.

capabilities.name: Release PR auto-merge
capabilities.behavior: When release-please returns a non-empty `pr` output, the auto-merge-release job mints a `glycemicgpt-merge` App token (MERGE_APP_ID / MERGE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, resolvable only inside `release-gated`), extracts the first integer from the PR output with `grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1`, and runs `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. No content validation on this PR (unlike the changelog and sync merges) — the trust anchor is that release-please authored it and the environment approval gate fired. If no numeric PR id can be parsed it prints "No PR number found" and exits successfully.

capabilities.name: Deployable-change detection for the fallback release
capabilities.behavior: Runs only for a promotion merge that produced neither a release nor a release PR. Checks out with `fetch-depth: 2`, diffs `git diff --name-only <sha>^1 <sha>` (merge commit vs first parent = main before merge), and greps the changed paths against `^(app/|wear-device/|watchface/|plugins/|gradle/|gradlew|settings\.gradle\.kts|settings-gradle\.lockfile|build\.gradle\.kts|gradle\.properties)`. Any match sets `has_deployable_changes=true`. Deliberate decision: doc-only promotions (README, GOVERNANCE, CLAUDE.md, docs/) must NOT cut a versioned signed release, so they produce no output and the fallback job is skipped.

capabilities.name: Fallback patch release
capabilities.behavior: Covers a promotion whose commits are all chore/ci/docs/test (release-please skips) but which changed deployable code. Reads CURRENT from `git show <github.sha>:.release-please-manifest.json | jq -r '.["."]'` — read from the immutable triggering SHA so a rerun cannot compute a different version after the first run already bumped main. Splits on '.', increments PATCH, VERSION=M.m.p+1, TAG=vVERSION. If the tag already exists it sets `already_exists=true` and skips the bump. Otherwise it jq-rewrites the manifest, `sed`-rewrites `val appVersionName = "CURRENT"` -> VERSION in the three module build.gradle.kts, and greps each file to verify the rewrite (hard fail otherwise). Git identity is `glycemicgpt-release[bot] <glycemicgpt-release[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.
edge_cases: Idempotent rerun: if nothing is staged (`git diff --cached --quiet`) it skips the commit rather than aborting, so tag/release steps can still finish a run that died after the push.
`git pull --rebase origin main` before pushing; on conflict it aborts the rebase and fails the job.

`git push --atomic origin main refs/tags/$TAG` — branch and lightweight tag land together or not at all; `--follow-tags` would not push a lightweight tag and letting `gh release create` mint the tag would anchor it to whatever main HEAD is.

Rerun path: if the tag exists but no GitHub Release does (a run died between push and release), the job creates the Release from the existing tag with `--verify-tag`, then reports release_created=true.

capabilities.name: Release APK build and asset naming
capabilities.behavior: Checks out the release tag with `persist-credentials: false`, JDK 17 (temurin), gradle/actions/setup-gradle v6.2.0, loads release signing from 1Password, then: `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease` (required, fails the job), `:wear-device:assembleRelease` and `:watchface:assembleRelease` both with `continue-on-error: true`. Renames by `find`+`head -1`: `GlycemicGPT-${VERSION}-release.apk` (phone, missing = hard error), `GlycemicGPT-Wear-${VERSION}-release.apk` (missing = warning only here), `GlycemicGPT-WatchFace-Digital-${VERSION}-release.apk` from `watchface/build/outputs/apk/digitalFull/release`, `GlycemicGPT-WatchFace-Analog-${VERSION}-release.apk` from `analogMechanical/release`. Uploads all with `gh release upload $TAG GlycemicGPT-*-release.apk --clobber` using a fresh glycemicgpt-release token, and also as workflow artifact `release-apk`, retention 90 days. `if: always()` step rm's the materialized keystore.
edge_cases: Wear build failure is tolerated at build time (so its own step reports the failure) but is fatal at the cert-verification step, per parity-gate global rule 4.
VERSION in the asset filename is always MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH — the in-app updater's anchored regex depends on it.

capabilities.name: Release signing-certificate assertion
capabilities.behavior: Hardcoded `RELEASE_SIGNER_SHA256=55f0d0cdabf20b398ad30a0ce3e998e3192666e5c15e6d378b86e1c8de342990` in the job env. Resolves apksigner from the highest `$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/*` by `sort -V | tail -1`, falling back to `apksigner` on PATH. For phone AND wear (both required; missing file = hard error) it runs `apksigner verify --print-certs`, greps `SHA-256 digest`, extracts `[0-9a-fA-F]{64}`, lowercases, takes the first, and fails the job on mismatch or empty. Reason this exists: both release buildTypes silently fall back to the DEBUG signing config when `RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE` is unset, so without this assertion a debug-signed 'release' would reach users. WatchFace APKs are deliberately excluded — they are unsigned/debug-signed by long-standing pre-split behavior and users consume the committed in-app WFF assets instead.
edge_cases: `|| true` on the digest pipeline is intentional so an unmatched grep under `set -euo pipefail` doesn't bypass the friendlier ::error:: message; apksigner's own stderr still reaches the log.
APK filenames are routed through `env:` (PHONE_APK/WEAR_APK) rather than interpolated into the shell source, to avoid template injection.

capabilities.name: Gradle signingConfigs and the debug-fallback
capabilities.behavior: All three modules read signing entirely from environment variables — no keystore path or password is in the repo. debug config is only overridden when `DEBUG_KEYSTORE_FILE` is non-blank; then `DEBUG_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`/`DEBUG_KEY_ALIAS`/`DEBUG_KEY_PASSWORD` are `requireNotNull` with explicit messages. Local dev with no env falls back to `~/.android/debug.keystore`. `release` config is populated from `RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE`/`_PASSWORD`, `RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS`/`RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD`. In app and wear-device the release buildType chooses `signingConfigs.getByName("release")` if `RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE != null`, else `"debug"` — the silent fallback. watchface's release buildType unconditionally uses the debug config (documented: a dedicated release keystore comes when production distribution is set up; Watch Face Push does not enforce Play Store signing) and sets `vcsInfo { include = false }`.

capabilities.name: op-load-signing-secrets composite action
capabilities.behavior: Input `keystore` must be exactly `release` or `debug` (validated, else ::error). Requires `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` in the calling job env; fail-closed with a pointer to docs/dev/signing-and-secrets.md if unset. Installs the 1Password CLI (1password/install-cli-action v4.0.0, SHA a5215d3a7f75c1629216c465ea9ab3ab399c4b71), then uses 1password/load-secrets-action v4.0.1 (SHA 3a12b0ab99d9cd590a3e9b5a90ea017210ed9556, `export-env: true`) to resolve the three text fields for the chosen identity into masked env vars. Materialize step: `umask 077`, `trap 'rm -f $dest' ERR`, `rm -f $dest`, `op read op://github/android-signing/<release.jks|debug.keystore> --out-file $RUNNER_TEMP/<name> --force`, `chmod 600`. Emits output `keystore-path` and writes `RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE`/`DEBUG_KEYSTORE_FILE` to `$GITHUB_ENV` (inline `# zizmor: ignore[github-env]`).
edge_cases: The action deliberately does NOT redeclare OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN: composite actions cannot read `secrets`, and redeclaring from an empty context would clobber the inherited value.
`--force` prevents a hang on the overwrite prompt on persistent/self-hosted runners.
Composite actions cannot register a post-job step, so callers must add their own `if: always()` rm of keystore-path.

capabilities.name: 1Password secret model
capabilities.behavior: Single source of truth: vault `github`, item `android-signing`; every reference is `op://github/android-signing/<name>`. File attachments (`release.jks`, `debug.keystore`) must be read with the op CLI — load-secrets-action cannot resolve attachments. Text fields: RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS, RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD, DEBUG_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, DEBUG_KEY_ALIAS, DEBUG_KEY_PASSWORD — names already match the Gradle env-var names, exported 1:1. Non-sensitive `canary` field = "ok". The ONLY signing-related GitHub secret is `ANDROID_ACTIONS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, a read-only service-account token scoped to that vault, mapped by callers to `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`. Stated guarantee: a leaked token can only read `android-signing`; rotation is a one-line GitHub-secret change with no keystore re-issuance. `*_KEYSTORE_FILE` is the only name the action synthesizes and is not itself secret.

capabilities.name: Signing plumbing smoke tests
capabilities.behavior: Two `workflow_dispatch`-only workflows, both `permissions: contents: read`. secrets-plumbing-check.yml installs only the op CLI and resolves ONLY `op://github/android-signing/canary`, asserting non-empty without echoing it; prints `1Password plumbing OK`. Run after token rotation. signing-action-smoke.yml runs the real composite action with `keystore: debug` and asserts three things: `DEBUG_KEYSTORE_FILE` was exported, the `keystore-path` output equals it, and the file exists and is non-empty (`-s`); prints only paths, never bytes. Both end with an `if: always()` keystore rm. Documented constraint: GitHub only exposes the Run-workflow control (and `gh workflow run`) once a workflow_dispatch workflow reaches the default branch `main`, so neither is dispatchable while it lives only on `develop`.

capabilities.name: GitHub App identity model
capabilities.behavior: Four Apps, all minted per-job with actions/create-github-app-token v3.2.0 (SHA bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1); the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN is never used for a write. `glycemicgpt-release` (RELEASE_APP_ID / RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY) — release-please, fallback version-bump push/tag/release, APK asset upload, changelog branch+PR. `glycemicgpt-merge` (MERGE_APP_ID / MERGE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY) — admin-merges the release PR, the changelog PR, and the sync PR. `glycemicgpt-ci` (CI_APP_ID / CI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY) — publishes dev-latest, labels PRs (best-effort, `continue-on-error`, falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN). `glycemicgpt-renovate` (RENOVATE_APP_ID / RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, `permission-contents: write` only) — pushes regenerated lockfiles. RELEASE and MERGE keys exist only as `release-gated` environment secrets, so every job that mints them pauses for required-reviewer approval.

capabilities.name: Changelog cutoff-marker windowing
capabilities.behavior: changelog-pr.yml runs on push to main / workflow_dispatch, `permissions: {}`, concurrency group `changelog-pr` (serialized, not cancelled — two same-day promotions would otherwise race the force-with-lease push on `changelog/<DATE>`). Job condition: (workflow_dispatch OR head_commit.message contains 'promote develop to main') AND NOT contains '[Changelog]' AND NOT contains 'chore: release'. Lower bound SINCE comes from `<!-- changelog-cutoff:<ISO8601> -->` in CHANGELOG.md, validated against `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}[Z+]` (hard fail otherwise, anti-injection). Fallbacks in order: last `## YYYY-MM-DD` or release-please `## [x.y.z](...) (YYYY-MM-DD)` header + 1 day at 00:00:00Z; else `2025-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Upper bound UNTIL = `github.event.head_commit.timestamp`, or `git log -1 --format=%cI origin/main` for dispatch; normalized to UTC; TODAY = its date part.

capabilities.name: Merged-PR collection via GraphQL
capabilities.behavior: Paginated GraphQL `search(type: ISSUE, first: 100, after: $cursor)` with query `repo:<owner/repo> is:pr is:merged base:develop merged:$SINCE..$UNTIL`, accumulating nodes (number, title, url, mergedAt, author.login, first 20 labels) until `pageInfo.hasNextPage` is false. Empty result -> `has_changes=false`, clean exit. Inclusion predicate `should_include`: a PR is kept if it carries any `keepLabels` entry (`dependencies`) OR carries none of `excludeLabels` (`automated`, `autorelease: tagged`, `autorelease: pending`, `invalid`). If everything filters out, `has_changes=false`.

capabilities.name: Changelog scope/sub-category taxonomy
capabilities.behavior: Two-dimensional jq categorization driven by `.github/changelog-pr-config.json`. Scopes in order (first label match wins; scope order also orders sections): Mobile 📱 [mobile, component: mobile], Wear OS ⌚ [wear], Watch Face 🎨 [watchface], Plugins 🔌 [plugin, plugins], Security 🔒 [security], CI & Build 🏗️ [ci, build, chore], Documentation 📚 [docs, documentation], Dependencies 📦 [dependencies], Uncategorized ❓ [needs triage]. First six have `hasSubCategories: true`. Sub-categories by ascending priority: Breaking Changes 💥 [breaking-change] p0, New Features ✨ [feature, enhancement] p1, Bug Fixes 🐛 [bugfix, bug] p2, Performance ⚡ [performance] p3, Refactor 🔧 [refactor] p4, default Other Changes 📝 p99. Rendering: `## <TODAY>`, `### <emoji> <Scope>`, optional `#### <emoji> <SubCat>`, entries `- <title> [@login](https://github.com/login) ([#n](url))`, then a fresh `<!-- changelog-cutoff:<NOW> -->`.
edge_cases: Unmatched scope falls back to the config's Uncategorized entry, or a hardcoded {name:"Uncategorized", emoji:"❓", hasSubCategories:false}.
Missing author.login renders as `ghost`.
Scopes not present in the config sort to index 999 (last).

capabilities.name: Changelog branch, commit, and PR
capabilities.behavior: Branch `changelog/<TODAY>`. Git identity `glycemicgpt-release[bot]`. Fetches any existing remote branch first (checkout only fetched main) so `--force-with-lease` has a remote-tracking basis, then `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` (always re-based on main). CHANGELOG.md update: if the file starts with a `# ` header, the new section is inserted after line 1 and the rest appended; if no `# ` header, prepended; if the file is absent, a `# Changelog` header is created. Commit `git commit -s -m "[Changelog] Update CHANGELOG.md for <TODAY>"` (DCO sign-off required), push with `--force-with-lease`. PR title is exactly `[Changelog] Update CHANGELOG.md`, base main. The PR number is parsed from `gh pr create`'s URL output (`grep -oE '[0-9]+$'`) rather than a follow-up `gh pr list`, which could race GitHub's eventual consistency and silently skip the merge job.

capabilities.name: Changelog PR validation and admin-merge
capabilities.behavior: merge-changelog job, `environment: release-gated`, `permissions: {}`, runs only when `has_changes == 'true' && pr_number != ''`. Mints the glycemicgpt-merge token, then re-reads the PR (`gh pr view --json author,title,files`) and enforces three guards before an `--admin` bypass: author must be `glycemicgpt-release[bot]` or `app/glycemicgpt-release` (gh and REST report different forms); title must equal `[Changelog] Update CHANGELOG.md` exactly; the changed-file list must contain nothing other than `CHANGELOG.md` (checked with `grep -v '^CHANGELOG\.md$'`). Any violation is a hard ::error exit 1. On pass: `gh pr review --approve` then `gh pr merge --rebase --admin` (rebase, not squash — squash is used for the release and sync PRs).

capabilities.name: Sync-back trigger and need-detection
capabilities.behavior: sync-main-to-develop.yml runs on push to main, `permissions: {}`, concurrency `sync-main-to-develop` (serialized), `environment: release-gated`. Job condition: head_commit.message contains `chore: release` OR `[Changelog] Update CHANGELOG.md` — feature commits from the promotion merge never match, so there is no loop. Checks out `develop` with the merge-bot token and `fetch-depth: 0`; identity `glycemicgpt-merge[bot]`. Need check: compare `.["."]` of `.release-please-manifest.json` on origin/main vs origin/develop. If they differ and the trigger is a `[Changelog]` commit, it skips (`needed=false`) so the version-bump sync lands first — an explicit ordering constraint. If versions match, it compares sha256 of CHANGELOG.md on both branches and skips if equal. It also skips if an open PR already exists on head `sync/main-to-develop-<7-char sha>`.

capabilities.name: Sync-back cherry-pick and conflict allowlist
capabilities.behavior: Branch `sync/main-to-develop-<sha[0:7]>` off origin/develop. PR title: `chore: sync release <X.Y.Z> from main to develop` when `grep -oP 'chore: release \K[0-9.]+'` matches, else `chore: sync changelog update from main to develop`. Runs `git cherry-pick <sha> --no-commit`. On conflict, only five files are force-resolved to main's version (`git show <sha>:<f> > <f>; git add <f>`): `.release-please-manifest.json`, `app/build.gradle.kts`, `wear-device/build.gradle.kts`, `watchface/build.gradle.kts`, `CHANGELOG.md`. If a listed file is absent from the source commit it falls back to `git checkout --theirs`. Any file still unresolved -> ::warning, `unresolved=true`, `git cherry-pick --abort`, nothing pushed, manual sync required. Stated rationale: only these files have an unambiguous 'main always wins' rule; CHANGELOG.md is in the list because release-please (release-type simple) owns it and would otherwise stall every version sync.

capabilities.name: Sync PR creation and admin-merge validation
capabilities.behavior: Commits with `git commit -s` (DCO), pushes the sync branch, and opens a PR against `develop` whose body records the source commit and notes whether conflicts were auto-resolved. Before `gh pr merge --squash --admin` it re-validates: author must be `glycemicgpt-merge[bot]` or `app/glycemicgpt-merge`; every changed file must match `^(\.release-please-manifest\.json|app/build\.gradle\.kts|wear-device/build\.gradle\.kts|watchface/build\.gradle\.kts|CHANGELOG\.md|\.release-please-changelog\.md)$`. Note the merge allowlist has six entries (it additionally tolerates `.release-please-changelog.md`) while the conflict resolver handles five — the sixth file does not exist in this repo. Any unexpected path is a hard failure; the guard is explicitly described as defense-in-depth because the PR was built in the same run from a trusted main commit.

capabilities.name: dev-latest pre-release channel
capabilities.behavior: dev-pre-release.yml runs on push to `develop` restricted to paths app/**, wear-device/**, watchface/**, plugins/**, gradle/**, gradlew, gradlew.bat, settings.gradle.kts, settings-gradle.lockfile, build.gradle.kts, gradle.properties, and its own workflow file. Concurrency `dev-pre-release` (serialized). `permissions: contents: read`. Loads DEBUG signing from 1Password (fail-closed: an unset service-account token fails before any build, so a dev APK is never published unsigned — there is no base64 keystore and no unsigned fallback). Builds `./gradlew assembleDebug -PdevBuildNumber=<N>`. Extracts VERSION by grepping `val appVersionName` from app/build.gradle.kts and rejects anything not matching `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`. Produces `dist/GlycemicGPT-<VERSION>-dev.<RUN>-debug.apk` and `dist/GlycemicGPT-Wear-<VERSION>-dev.<RUN>-debug.apk`; fails if dist/ ends up empty.

capabilities.name: DEV_RUN_NUMBER_OFFSET = 500 (permanent, do-not-remove)
capabilities.behavior: The published dev build number is `GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER + 500`. It is embedded twice: into `BuildConfig.DEV_BUILD_NUMBER` via `-PdevBuildNumber`, and into the release asset filename that `AppUpdateChecker.parseDevRunNumber` reads back. Reason: after the repo split this repo's run counter restarted near 0 while the monorepo-built cohort already had dev.145 installed; the updater's strictly-greater comparison would report 'up to date' forever and strand every migrated dev user. Explicit decision recorded in the workflow: the offset is PERMANENT. Because every published number is native+500, the native counter can never catch up (at native 146 the published number is 646); deleting the offset would publish 146 to devices holding 646 and strand them permanently. Retiring it requires a staged migration that keeps every new number above the highest ever emitted.

capabilities.name: dev-latest publish (delete-and-recreate)
capabilities.behavior: Mints a glycemicgpt-ci App token, then in one step runs `gh release delete dev-latest --yes --cleanup-tag 2>/dev/null || true` immediately followed by `gh release create dev-latest --title "<VERSION>-dev.<RUN>" --prerelease --target develop dist/*.apk`. Both commands are in the same step explicitly to minimize the window where no dev-latest exists. Release notes embed VERSION-dev.RUN, the 7-char commit SHA, branch develop, and a pointer to the latest stable release. Final `if: always()` step removes the materialized keystore. During the delete/create window the in-app dev updater's GitHub call returns 404, which the client maps to the message 'No dev release available yet.' rather than an error state.
edge_cases: `--cleanup-tag` deletes the dev-latest tag too, so the tag is recreated pointing at the newest develop head each run.
A failed create after a successful delete leaves the dev channel with no release until the next push.

capabilities.name: In-app phone update channel client
capabilities.behavior: `AppUpdateChecker` selects endpoint by `BuildConfig.UPDATE_CHANNEL` (`"dev"` for the debug buildType, `"stable"` for release): dev -> `https://api.github.com/repos/lumose-health/android-unofficial/releases/tags/dev-latest`, stable -> `.../releases/latest`. OkHttp connectTimeout 15s, readTimeout 60s. HTTP 403 -> 'Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.'; 404 on dev -> 'No dev release available yet.'. Asset selection is anchored and fails closed: stable `^GlycemicGPT-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)-release\.apk$` with the captured version required to equal `tagName` minus 'v'; dev `^GlycemicGPT-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)-dev\.\d+-debug\.apk$`; `matches.singleOrNull()` so ambiguity returns null ('No APK found in release'). Comparison: dev uses `parseDevRunNumber(name) > BuildConfig.DEV_BUILD_NUMBER` (regex `-dev\.(\d+)-`, 0 on no match); stable uses `parseVersionCode(version) > currentVersionCode` with the same major*1_000_000 + minor*10_000 + patch formula.
edge_cases: A stale asset from another release (e.g. GlycemicGPT-1.2.2-release.apk attached to v1.2.3) is rejected by the expectedVersion check.
Anchoring exists because Wear and WatchFace APKs share the phone applicationId and signing key — picking one would install it in place OVER the phone app.

capabilities.name: APK download hardening
capabilities.behavior: Before any download: `isHttpsUrl` requires a hierarchical `https://` URI with a non-empty host (rejects opaque `https:payload`), enforced in code rather than relying on network_security_config because the base config permits cleartext for the LAN opt-in; `isAllowedDownloadHost` allows only `github.com` and `objects.githubusercontent.com` plus their subdomains (`host == allowed || host.endsWith("."+allowed)`). Filename is sanitized (strip after `?` and `#`, replace `[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]` with `_`, empty -> `update.apk`). Old APKs in `cacheDir/apk_updates` are deleted first. After download, if `expectedSize > 0` and the file length differs, the file is deleted and an error returned. Install uses FileProvider authority `<packageName>.fileprovider` with ACTION_VIEW, mime `application/vnd.android.package-archive`, FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION + FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK.

capabilities.name: Wear APK update client
capabilities.behavior: `WearAppUpdateChecker` polls the same two GitHub endpoints, choosing suffix `-debug.apk` for dev and `-release.apk` for stable, and selects the first asset with prefix `GlycemicGPT-Wear-` and that suffix (`firstOrNull`, not the anchored/single-match discipline the phone selector uses). Dev compares `AppUpdateChecker.parseDevRunNumber(name) > watchDevBuildNumber`; stable compares `AppUpdateChecker.parseVersionCode(tag minus 'v') > watchVersionCode`. Cache subdir `wear_apk_updates`. `MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_BYTES = 100L * 1024 * 1024` (100 MB) guards disk exhaustion. CancellationException is rethrown rather than swallowed; other exceptions become `UpdateCheckResult.Error`. Same 403/404 message mapping as the phone checker.

capabilities.name: Gradle dependency locking
capabilities.behavior: Root build.gradle.kts applies `dependencyLocking { lockAllConfigurations() }` to allprojects, so every module commits a `gradle.lockfile` (app, wear-device, watchface, plugins/pump-driver-api, plugins/shipped/{tandem,medtronic}, tools/medtronic-ble-spike) plus a root `settings-gradle.lockfile`. Two configuration families are excluded via `resolutionStrategy.deactivateDependencyLocking()`: names starting `_internal-unified-test-platform` (AGP's bundled instrumented-test host tooling — pinned by AGP, never shipped, only movable by an AGP bump, so locking would put AGP's supply chain on the CVE gate with unfixable findings) and names ending `DependenciesMetadata` (Kotlin compile-metadata views, not real classpaths). Custom task `resolveAndLockAll` requires `--write-locks`, resolves only `incoming.resolutionResult.root` per resolvable configuration, and rethrows any resolution failure that is not in the excluded set. Regenerate manually with `./gradlew resolveAndLockAll --write-locks`.

capabilities.name: Lockfile regeneration for Renovate PRs
capabilities.behavior: regen-gradle-lockfiles.yml exists because Renovate's container has no Android SDK. Trigger: pull_request opened/synchronize on paths gradle/libs.versions.toml, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties, `**/build.gradle.kts`. Concurrency per PR number, cancel-in-progress true. Guards (all three): author == `glycemicgpt-renovate[bot]`, head repo == this repo (no forks), head ref starts with `renovate/`. Two-job privilege split. `regenerate` (timeout 15 min, no credential ever, `cache-read-only: true` so PR build scripts cannot poison the shared cache) checks out the head ref, records the exact SHA, runs `./gradlew resolveAndLockAll --write-locks --console=plain`, counts `git status --porcelain -- '*gradle.lockfile'`, and uploads `settings-gradle.lockfile` + `**/gradle.lockfile` as artifact `gradle-lockfiles` (`if-no-files-found: error`, retention 1 day).
edge_cases: tools/medtronic-ble-spike is intentionally not regenerated (outside Renovate's ignorePaths scope).
The push retriggers the workflow once via `synchronize`; the second run produces no diff and exits.
Documented as an UNPROVEN PATH — Renovate is not yet installed, so it has never fired.

capabilities.name: Privileged lockfile push job
capabilities.behavior: `push` job (timeout 5 min) runs only when `changed != '0'`. It checks out the EXACT SHA the lockfiles were built from with `persist-credentials: false`, downloads the artifact over the tree, then mints a glycemicgpt-renovate token scoped `permission-contents: write` (without which it would inherit every installation permission). Sets `git config core.hooksPath /dev/null` (so no PR-authored hook runs), identity `glycemicgpt-renovate[bot]`, `git add -- '*gradle.lockfile'`, exits with a ::notice if nothing is staged, else commits `chore(deps): refresh gradle lockfiles` with `--signoff` and pushes `HEAD:<head ref>` via `https://x-access-token:$TOKEN@github.com/<repo>.git`. The non-force push to a pinned SHA means that if Renovate advanced the branch meanwhile, the push is rejected as non-fast-forward rather than committing lockfiles that no longer match the build files. This job never executes PR code.

capabilities.name: Renovate global policy
capabilities.behavior: renovate.json5 extends config:recommended, :dependencyDashboard, :semanticCommits, helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests. `baseBranchPatterns: ["develop"]` (main is promotion-only). GUARD: top-level `automerge: false` — platformAutomerge defaults true, so any rule setting automerge:true would enqueue native auto-merge at PR creation and bypass the workflow file allowlist. automergeStrategy squash; branchPrefix `renovate/`; semanticCommitType `chore`, scope `deps`. DCO: `gitAuthor: "glycemicgpt-renovate[bot] <272302492+glycemicgpt-renovate[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>"` and `commitBody: "Signed-off-by: {{{gitAuthor}}}"` (triple braces so `<email>` is not HTML-escaped). prHourlyLimit 3, prConcurrentLimit 6. `minimumReleaseAge: "7 days"` + `internalChecksFilter: "strict"` — the PR is not even opened until the soak passes. `lockFileMaintenance` disabled. labels `[dependencies]`. `ignorePaths: ["tools/**"]`. `ignoreDeps: ["int:DEV_BUILD_NUMBER"]` (false positive from a buildConfigField). timezone America/Chicago, schedule 'after 9am and before 5pm every weekday'.

capabilities.name: Renovate tiers and never-auto-merge set
capabilities.behavior: Tier B (the only rule adding `automerge`): matchManagers gradle, matchDepTypes [dependencies], matchUpdateTypes [patch, minor], all-negative matchPackageNames excluding by VENDOR GLOB `org.bouncycastle:*`, `net.zetetic:*`, `androidx.security:*`, `org.openminimed:*` (so a future sibling artifact like bcpkix or security-crypto-ktx cannot slip through) plus `com.google.dagger:hilt-android(-compiler)`, `com.github.jeziellago:compose-markdown`, `androidx.wear.watchface:watchface-push`, `...validator-push-android`, and the six plugin ids. Tier D rules are placed AFTER Tier B so `labels` last-wins, and none adds `automerge`: build-toolchain (gradle plugins, plugin ids, Dagger-Hilt libs, gradle-wrapper), all majors, crypto/cipher (patch/minor and major variants), JitPack markdown, wear watchface prerelease alphas, and all GitHub Actions bumps incl. digest re-pins. Grouping rules that can hold an auto-eligible package are all scoped [patch,minor] and exclude manual coordinates by name.
edge_cases: Deliberate safe-fail: if Gradle does not tag catalog libraries with the `dependencies` depType, Tier B matches nothing and EVERYTHING falls to manual review.
Renovate 43 rejects mixing a bare `*` with other patterns, hence the all-negative form.

`androidx.hilt:hilt-navigation-compose` is capped at `allowedVersions: "[,1.2.0]"` — Gradle constraint syntax, because a SemVer `<=1.2.0` matches nothing under Renovate's gradle versioning and would let lint-breaking 1.3.0 through.

CVE paths (`osvVulnerabilityAlerts: true`, `vulnerabilityAlerts` with labels [security, dependencies]) bypass the soak and the rate limits, but arrive labeled `security`, which the auto-merge guards treat as manual-only.

capabilities.name: Renovate label-relay and its missing workflow
capabilities.behavior: Documented design: Renovate never merges; it labels, and `auto-merge-renovate.yml` relays a safe subset to GitHub native auto-merge with `gh pr merge --auto --squash`, and runs `gh pr merge --disable-auto` when a PR loses eligibility (native auto-merge is otherwise sticky and a label change alone never cancels it). Guards (all required): author == glycemicgpt-renovate[bot]; base branch develop, never main; `automerge` label present; and NONE of `security`, `needs-review`, `major`, `build-toolchain`, `security-sensitive`, `prerelease`, `ci-actions`. IMPORTANT DIVERGENCE: `.github/workflows/auto-merge-renovate.yml` does not exist in this repository, although both docs/dev/dependency-updates.md and zizmor.yml's `dangerous-triggers` allowlist name it. The relay is therefore absent here; only the File Scope check and the Renovate config side of the design are present.

capabilities.name: Renovate File Scope required check
capabilities.behavior: pull_request_target on branches [main, develop], types opened/synchronize/reopened/labeled/unlabeled; `permissions: pull-requests: read`; per-PR concurrency, cancel-in-progress true; timeout 5 min. No checkout and no PR code — it reads the PR file list via `gh api --paginate repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>/files`. No-op PASS unless author == glycemicgpt-renovate[bot] AND the `automerge` label is present. Then each changed file must (a) not be under `tools/*` (rejected first, before the generic Gradle patterns, because no gate builds it), (b) match ALLOWLIST_RE `^((.*/)?build\.gradle\.kts|(.*/)?gradle\.lockfile|gradle/libs\.versions\.toml|settings\.gradle\.kts|settings-gradle\.lockfile)$`, and (c) match GATE_RE, the union of the Android Gate and Dependency Scan Gate paths-filters. A file that is allowlisted but outside gate coverage would auto-merge unbuilt and unscanned, so it fails too. Any violation exits 1 with instructions to remove the label.
edge_cases: pull_request_target is deliberate so the gate evaluates its own trusted base-branch logic, not a version the PR could have edited.
Security Scan Gate has no paths-filter, so it contributes nothing to GATE_RE and cannot close the coverage gap.

capabilities.name: Renovate config validator
capabilities.behavior: renovate-config-validator.yml runs on PRs to main/develop that touch `renovate.json5` or the workflow itself, plus workflow_dispatch. `permissions: contents: read`, timeout 5 min, per-ref concurrency with cancel-in-progress. Node major pinned to `'24'` (Renovate 43 requires Node >= 24.11). Runs `npx --yes --package "renovate@43.260.2" renovate-config-validator --strict` with NO file argument — deliberate, so the validator auto-discovers renovate.json5 at the repo root and validates it as REPO config (the exact path the Renovate app resolves) rather than the superset 'global config' check an explicit file path triggers. `--strict` fails on deprecations and required schema migrations, not just hard errors; RENOVATE_VERSION is pinned so the schema is reproducible.

capabilities.name: Auto-labeling (feeds changelog + Renovate policy)
capabilities.behavior: auto-label.yml runs on pull_request_target (main, develop; opened/synchronize/reopened/edited), job permissions `contents: read` + `pull-requests: write`. Mints a glycemicgpt-ci token best-effort (`continue-on-error`, falls back to `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, which has write scope under pull_request_target). Installs `minimatch@10.0.3` pinned exactly with `--no-save --no-package-lock --no-fund --no-audit --ignore-scripts`. Path labels from `.github/autolabeler-config.json`: mobile=app/**, wear=wear-device/**, watchface=watchface/**, plugin=plugins/**, ci=.github/**, docs=docs/**+**/*.md excluding CHANGELOG.md, dependencies=gradle/libs.versions.toml+**/gradle.lockfile+settings-gradle.lockfile+renovate.json5, security=.github/workflows/*security*.yml+SECURITY.md+osv-scanner.toml. Title labels from `^(\w+)(\(.+\))?!?:` mapped feat->feature, fix->bugfix, docs->documentation, style, refactor, perf->performance, test->tests, build, ci, chore, revert. Adds `breaking-change` on `!:` in the title or a `(^|\n)\s*BREAKING[ -]CHANGE:` body footer. Empty label set -> `needs triage`.
edge_cases: listFiles is paginated at per_page 100 — unpaginated it would label from only the first 30 files and mis-categorize the changelog.
The `(^|\n)\s*` anchor prevents 'non-breaking change' from matching.
Label add failures are caught and logged, not fatal.

capabilities.name: commit-msg git hook
capabilities.behavior: `.githooks/commit-msg`, installed with `cp .githooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x` or `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Git runs only one commit-msg hook, so both policies live in one file. Job 1 strips AI attribution: deletes `Co-Authored-By:` lines matching the alternation `[Cc]laude|[Aa]nthropic|[Cc]opilot|[Cc]hat[Gg][Pp][Tt]|[Oo]pen[Aa][Ii]|[Cc]ursor|[Ww]indsurf|[Cc]odeium|[Cc]ode[Ww]hisperer|[Aa]mazon\.[Qq]|[Gg]emini|[Jj]et[Bb]rains\.[Aa][Ii]|[Tt]abnine|[Ss]ourcegraph|[Cc]ody|[Dd]evin|[Aa]ider|[Cc]odex|\[bot\]|noreply@`, then deletes any `Authored-By:`/`Generated-By:`/`AI-Generated-By:` trailer, then collapses trailing blank lines with `perl -0777 -pi -e 's/\n{2,}\z/\n/'` (character classes and perl chosen for macOS/Linux portability). Job 2 warns (non-blocking) when `^Signed-off-by: .+ <.+@.+>$` is absent, pointing at `git commit -s` / `--amend -s --no-edit`. Always exits 0.

capabilities.name: DCO enforcement
capabilities.behavior: `.github/dco.yml` configures the DCO GitHub App: `require.members: true` (no exemption tier — maintainers and the project lead sign off like anyone else) and `allowRemediationCommits.individual: true` (one `chore: DCO remediation` commit can fix a whole branch's history instead of rewriting every commit). Server-side, it blocks any PR containing an unsigned commit regardless of whether the local hook is installed. Consequences across the pipeline: every bot commit is signed too — the changelog commit and the sync commit use `git commit -s`, the lockfile regen commit uses `--signoff`, and Renovate's own bump commit is signed via `gitAuthor` + `commitBody` in renovate.json5. The regen `--signoff` covers only its own commit, never Renovate's. Explicitly DCO, not a CLA: it grants no relicensing rights.

capabilities.name: CODEOWNERS routing for release automation
capabilities.behavior: Single owner `@jlengelbrecht` for `*` and, explicitly re-stated (later rules win), for: /.github/CODEOWNERS, GOVERNANCE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, LICENSE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md, /.github/dco.yml, ALL of /.github/workflows/ (plus release.yml named again), renovate.json5, release-please-config.json, .release-please-manifest.json, .github/changelog-pr-config.json, .github/autolabeler-config.json, zizmor.yml, gradle/libs.versions.toml, and the three safety-critical plugin trees (/plugins/pump-driver-api/, /plugins/shipped/tandem/, /plugins/shipped/medtronic/). Stated reasons: workflow files run with repo secrets and bypass-actor write access; a careless edit to the promotion config can mis-version a release, corrupt the changelog, or silently widen the workflow-security allowlist. Bot PRs from release-please and the sync workflow reach these paths via bypass actors, but required status checks still gate the merge.

capabilities.name: License policy gate on redistributed dependencies
capabilities.behavior: Root build.gradle.kts configures cash/licensee once for all subprojects (`unusedAction(UnusedAction.IGNORE)`, since one policy serves three modules with different graphs). Allowed SPDX: Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ICU, SAX-PD, SAX-PD-2.0. Allowed by URL: the GPL-3.0 text (this project's own licence) and `http://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-2-Clause` (commonmark 0.13.0 predates SPDX in its POM). EPL-1.0 is deliberately ABSENT: the FSF considers it incompatible with GPLv3 for a combined distributed work and this app is GPL-3.0-only; the one EPL artifact that reached the graph (an XPath 2.0 processor transitive of the alpha wear watchface validator) is excluded at that dependency in wear-device/build.gradle.kts, with WatchFaceValidatorTest proving the validator still works. Per-version `allowDependency` entries (Play services 18.x, TwelveMonkeys 3.9.4, java-cup 10k, sqlcipher 4.13.0, bcprov-jdk18on 1.84, three JitPack artifacts) each carry a `because` reason; a version bump re-raises the judgement.

capabilities.name: Dependency CVE scanning
capabilities.behavior: dependency-scan.yml uses dorny/paths-filter v4.0.2 with filter `deps`: `**/build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `**/gradle.lockfile`, `settings-gradle.lockfile`, `osv-scanner.toml`, and its own workflow file. Scans when the filter hits, or on schedule/workflow_dispatch. Installs `github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@v2.3.3` from source on the runner's Go toolchain (no third-party action to pin). Runs `osv-scanner scan --lockfile=gradle.lockfile:settings-gradle.lockfile --recursive --no-ignore --config=osv-scanner.toml .` — the parse-as hint is needed because the root lockfile has a non-standard basename, and `--no-ignore` stops `--recursive` honoring .gitignore so a lockfile can never be silently dropped while the gate stays green. osv-scanner.toml ships with NO active [[IgnoredVulns]]; first-scan triage over ~1,175 resolved packages found nothing. Suppressions require a written reason and an `ignoreUntil` forcing re-evaluation; quarterly review.

capabilities.name: Workflow hygiene gates guarding the pipeline
capabilities.behavior: workflow-lint.yml (push+PR on main/develop, timeout 5 min) installs SHA-256-verified pinned binaries rather than actions: shellcheck 0.10.0 (sha256 6c881ab0698e4e6ea235245f22832860544f17ba386442fe7e9d629f8cbedf87) and actionlint 1.7.7 (sha256 023070a287cd8cccd71515fedc843f1985bf96c436b7effaecce67290e7e0757); runs `actionlint -oneline -shellcheck=...`, a guard requiring every third-party `uses:` to pin a full 40-hex SHA (local `./` and docker refs exempt), and a composite-action guard against `${{ secrets.* }}` inside an action definition (which silently resolves to empty). workflow-security.yml installs `zizmor==1.5.2` + `pyyaml==6.0.2` and runs `zizmor --config zizmor.yml --min-severity=medium` over workflows AND composite actions — any Medium-or-higher finding not allowlisted fails. Policy: add a scoped zizmor.yml entry with a rationale; never lower the threshold. A companion guard fails any pull_request_target workflow that checks out PR head code.
edge_cases: zizmor.yml `dangerous-triggers` whole-file ignores: auto-merge-renovate.yml (absent from the repo), renovate-file-scope.yml, auto-label.yml, attribution-check.yml.
`artipacked` is line-scoped to exactly three credential-persisting checkouts that must push: changelog-pr.yml:49, sync-main-to-develop.yml:43, release.yml:154.
The op-load-signing-secrets `github-env` finding is suppressed inline at the step, not in zizmor.yml, so it survives line shifts.

capabilities.name: Local developer tooling (scripts/mobile-dev.sh)
capabilities.behavior: Bash helper, `set -euo pipefail`. Resolves adb from `$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb` then PATH (hard error if neither) and emulator from `$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator` then PATH. AVD name `test_device`. Artifact paths: `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`, `wear-device/build/outputs/apk/debug/wear-device-debug.apk`. Commands: devices; build (`./gradlew assembleDebug`); emulator start (`-no-audio -gpu auto`, backgrounded+disowned) / stop (`adb emu kill`) / install; phone install|logcat|ble-raw; watch install|logcat. Device selection: emulator = first serial matching `^emulator-`; phone = first non-emulator serial; watch = `$WATCH_SERIAL` if set, else first IP-shaped serial (WiFi-paired, e.g. 10.x.x.x:5555). phone logcat filters BleConnectionManager, TandemBleDriver, PumpPollingOrchestrator, JpakeAuthenticator, TandemAuthenticator at :D with `*:S`; ble-raw greps `BLE_RAW`; watch logcat filters the wear services and complication data sources.

capabilities.name: Build-time toolchain and flags relevant to release artifacts
capabilities.behavior: Gradle wrapper 8.12 (`gradle-8.12-bin.zip`), AGP 8.7.3, Kotlin 2.1.0, KSP 2.1.0-1.0.29, Hilt 2.53.1, licensee 1.14.1, compose-bom 2024.12.01. Java 17 source/target and jvmTarget across CI and Gradle. app: namespace/applicationId `com.glycemicgpt.mobile`, compileSdk 35, minSdk 30, targetSdk 35. debug buildType: `applicationIdSuffix ".debug"`, `versionNameSuffix "-debug"`, `UPDATE_CHANNEL="dev"`, `DEV_BUILD_NUMBER` from `-PdevBuildNumber` (default 0). release buildType: minify + shrinkResources on, `UPDATE_CHANNEL="stable"`, `DEV_BUILD_NUMBER=0`. `MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED` defaults true and is only disabled by env `MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED=false` (kill switch: plugin becomes invisible/inert — not selectable, no pairing, no polling). Watch-face asset SHA-256s are computed at build time from committed APK assets into BuildConfig for a runtime tamper check.

capabilities.name: Sentry DSN exclusion from published artifacts
capabilities.behavior: Debug buildType reads a Sentry DSN from env `SENTRY_DSN` (blank treated as absent) or `-PsentryDsn`, defaulting to empty so Sentry stays disabled. Hard guard: if the DSN is non-empty AND `System.getenv("CI") == "true"`, the build throws a GradleException — because the debug APK is published as the downloadable `dev-latest` asset and a baked-in DSN is client-extractable. Release buildType hardcodes `SENTRY_DSN=""` and `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT="production"`; debug defaults the environment to `"development"`. Values are emitted through a `toJavaStringLiteral` helper escaping backslash and quote so an unusual value cannot break the generated Java literal.

safety_critical: Release signing certificate assertion (release.yml): both app and wear-device release buildTypes SILENTLY fall back to the debug signing config when RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE is unset. The only thing preventing a debug-signed 'release' APK reaching patients is the post-build apksigner check against RELEASE_SIGNER_SHA256=55f0d0cdabf20b398ad30a0ce3e998e3192666e5c15e6d378b86e1c8de342990. A debug-signed release cannot be installed as an upgrade over a properly signed install, and worse, a debug-key APK is trivially forgeable by a third party — anyone can build and sign an impostor update. Any Swift/iOS port must keep an equivalent hard fail rather than a warning.

versionCode derivation `major*1_000_000 + minor*10_000 + patch` is used identically in all three Gradle modules AND in AppUpdateChecker.parseVersionCode. It collides silently when patch > 9999 or minor > 99. A collision makes `remoteVersionCode > currentVersionCode` false and the app reports 'up to date' forever — patients would never receive a safety fix.

DEV_RUN_NUMBER_OFFSET=500 is load-bearing and permanent. The updater uses a strictly-greater comparison on the run number parsed out of the asset filename; removing or lowering the offset publishes numbers below what devices already hold and permanently strands dev-channel users on a stale build (no further updates, including safety fixes).

Phone APK asset selection is anchored (`^GlycemicGPT-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)-release\.apk$` / `-dev\.\d+-debug\.apk$`) and uses singleOrNull. Wear and WatchFace APKs share the phone's applicationId and signing key; if the selector matched one, Android would install it IN PLACE OVER the phone app, replacing the CGM/pump app with a watch binary. The stable channel additionally requires the embedded version to equal the release tag, so a stale asset cannot be installed under a version the user was told about.

APK download path is a code-execution path: https-only enforced in code (not just network_security_config, which permits cleartext for the LAN opt-in), host allowlist {github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com} incl. subdomains, filename sanitization, and an exact expected-size check that deletes a mismatched file. The wear checker caps downloads at 100 MB (100*1024*1024).

Renovate never-auto-merge set covers crypto/at-rest by VENDOR GLOB (org.bouncycastle:*, net.zetetic:* [SQLCipher], androidx.security:*, org.openminimed:* [Medtronic Sake crypto]) so a future sibling artifact cannot slip past. Doc reason: a silent behavior change here can weaken encryption of patient data without failing a build. Nothing in CI inspects dependency bytecode — the 7-day minimumReleaseAge soak is the primary supply-chain defense.

CODEOWNERS routes /plugins/pump-driver-api/, /plugins/shipped/tandem/, /plugins/shipped/medtronic/ to the project lead as 'safety-critical BLE parsing and SafetyLimits enforcement'. Any dependency or toolchain change reaching those trees must not auto-merge.

The label-relay's documented residual risk: auto-merge eligibility is decided from the PR's CURRENT label set, so anyone with GitHub Triage or higher could strip needs-review/security-sensitive from a crypto bump and add `automerge`. Accepted and contained only operationally (restrict Triage to trusted maintainers). A provenance-based tier derivation is explicitly deferred.

WatchFace release APKs are debug-signed (watchface release buildType unconditionally uses signingConfigs.getByName("debug")) and are deliberately excluded from the cert assertion. They are published as GitHub release assets. The stated mitigation is that users consume the committed in-app WFF assets, whose SHA-256 is compiled into BuildConfig and checked at runtime by WatchFacePusher.

Debug/`dev-latest` builds are signed with a real shared debug keystore from 1Password and are publicly downloadable. The fail-closed design (composite action aborts before any build if OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN is unset) is what prevents an unsigned or locally-keyed dev APK from being published.
The CI Sentry-DSN guard (GradleException when SENTRY_DSN is set and CI=true) prevents an extractable telemetry credential from shipping in the downloadable debug APK of a medical app.
Licensee EPL-1.0 exclusion is a legal-compliance safety gate: this app is GPL-3.0-only and a new EPL dependency fails the build rather than shipping in a GPL binary.

APK signing (apksigner, v1/v2/v3 signature schemes) is the trust anchor for both the release channel and the sideloaded update path; there is no Play Store distribution.

Filesystem: keystores materialized to $RUNNER_TEMP at mode 0600 (umask 077); downloaded APKs land in the app's cacheDir subdirs apk_updates / wear_apk_updates and old ones are deleted before each download.

Branch protection assumptions (documented go-live steps, not enforced in-repo): glycemicgpt-merge registered as a pull-request-only bypass actor on develop that must NOT be able to bypass required status checks; 'Renovate File Scope' registered as a required check; Dependency graph + Dependabot alerts enabled; Triage/label management restricted to trusted maintainers.

DIVERGENCES BETWEEN DOCS AND CODE — load-bearing for a port:
